inputs.share_count_basis: Q2 2026 10-Q diluted weighted-average shares (282.2m for the quarter ended 2026-06-30; basic 280.7m). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; buybacks (FY2025 $783.8m, H1 2026 $669.3m) are the cash mechanism that keeps the count flat and are value-neutral here.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement ShareBasedCompensation add-back ($136.6m). Cash taxes on net-share settlement are not tagged in the SEC XBRL (PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation absent) so no equity-award tax is added; SBC is therefore modestly understated.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows discounted at a USD WACC of 8.0%: 10-year UST ~4.1%, equity beta ~0.95, ERP 4.75% -> cost of equity ~8.6%; pre-tax cost of debt ~4.8% (A-/BBB+ senior notes issued 2025-26) -> ~3.8% after tax; weights ~86% equity / 14% debt on a $79bn market cap against ~$12.8bn pro-forma net debt. The same WACC is used in all three scenarios so that risk is charged once, through the probability weights, not twice.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A): US GAAP operating-lease cost (liability $761m at 2025-12-31, no finance leases tagged) is an operating expense inside EBITDA and EBIT, so lease liabilities are NOT added to net debt. One treatment only.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests are immaterial ($28.9m book at 2026-06-30, $17.7m of FY2025 net income). Flows are modelled on a consolidated basis and NCI is deducted once, at book, in the equity bridge.
inputs.coolit_treatment: CoolIT Systems (~$4.75bn cash, ~$550m run-rate revenue, close expected Q3 2026). The $5.08bn of notes issued in Q2 2026 to fund it is already in total_debt and the proceeds are in cash at 2026-06-30, so reported net debt is pre-payment. The purchase consideration is deducted in equity_bridge, and CoolIT revenue enters the flows from Y1 (roughly half a year) and annualises in Y2. If the deal breaks, remove both the bridge item and ~1.5pp from Y1 and ~2.5pp from Y2 growth.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 1: operating company). Ecolab is a USD filer and USD quote, no IFRS-16 split, no material NCI, SBC present at ~0.85% of revenue, so the adaptations file does not apply. Interest income ($65.1m in FY2025) is NOT stripped because the company is net-debt (~$8bn reported, ~$12.8bn pro-forma post-CoolIT), so there is no cash pile being double-counted. Year 1 is FY2026 (Dec year-end), which is three-quarters complete at the valuation date: H1 2026 reported revenue +9.9%, organic +5%, adjusted EPS guided $8.05-8.25, H2 organic guided 6-7% with adjusted operating margin ~19%. FY2024 reported operating income (17.8%) is inflated by the ~$0.5bn gain on the surgical-solutions divestiture in Q3 2024, so FY2025 (17.0% reported, ~17.9% adjusted) is the margin anchor. The June balance sheet already reflects H1 2026 cash generation and its use (buybacks, dividends); discounting the full FY2026 flow one period is the folder convention and is slightly conservative.

equity_bridge.item: CoolIT Systems purchase consideration (cash, closing Q3 2026; debt raised and sitting in cash at 30-Jun-26)
equity_bridge.note: Q2 2026 10-Q: $5,081.2m long-term debt issued; definitive agreement March 2026

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_5yr_cagr (6.4%) cross-checked against management's 5-7% organic algorithm; equity CAGR rejected as the anchor because buybacks and the FY2020 impairment distort book value
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (9.6%) exceeds revenue 5yr CAGR (6.4%) by ~50%: FY2020 book value was depressed by the $2.2bn ChampionX/goodwill impairment and the FY2020-25 rebuild is not a revenue signal. EPS 5yr CAGR is null because FY2020 EPS was -4.20; from FY2019 ($5.41) to FY2025 ($7.33) EPS compounded 5.2%/yr over six years.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC). 3yr FCF CAGR (21%) starts from the FY2022 working-capital trough ($1,076m reported) and overstates trend; the 5yr figure (6.5%) is the better read. Over five years SBC grew 10.7%/yr against 6.8% for reported FCF, so a rising share of reported growth is paid in stock; over three years the reverse held (SBC +15.9%/yr vs FCF +21%). Revenue history is depressed by divestitures (ChampionX separation June 2020, surgical solutions August 2024); organic growth ran 5-7% in 2023-26.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +10%: H1 reported +9.9% (organic 5%, FX/M&A ~5pp), H2 organic guided 6-7% plus ~half a year of CoolIT (~$250m, ~3pp of H2). FY2027 +8%: CoolIT annualises (~1.7pp) and grows, core organic 5.5%. Then the 5-7% organic algorithm fading to 4% by year 10.
base.margin_rationale: Adj EBITDA is pre-SBC (OI + D&A + SBC). FY2025 actual 23.95%. FY2026 24.5% = H1 reported OI 16.3% and H2 guided ~19% adjusted, plus D&A and SBC. Reaches 27.0% by FY2031, i.e. reported operating margin ~20% (27.0 - 0.85 SBC - 6.2 D&A), which is management's '20% by 2027' target delivered four years late; CoolIT is margin-dilutive in FY2027.
base.da_capex_rationale: D&A 6.07% in FY2025 (depreciation 672.6 + intangible amortisation 304.0); H1 2026 6.3%. Steps up to 6.7% in FY2027 for CoolIT acquisition intangibles then runs off to 6.0%. Capex 6.5% FY2025, 6.9% H1 2026 (High-Tech capacity), fading to 6.0% at maturity, equal to D&A.
base.tax_rationale: Cash taxes paid FY2025 $548.1m = 20.0% of EBIT ($2,737.6m) and 21.5% of pretax; GAAP ETR 17.8%. Unlevered NOPAT taxed at 20% ramping to 21%.
base.wc_rationale: Receivables (~19% of revenue) plus inventory (~10%) exceed payables (~10.5%) by roughly 15% of revenue, so each dollar of revenue growth consumes ~15c of working capital. FY2025 OCF ($2,952.6m) vs NI + D&A + SBC ($3,206.5m) shows ~$250m of working-capital and other absorption on $340m of revenue growth.

bull.rationale: CoolIT compounds at 25-30% for five years on the AI data-centre build-out and pulls Global Water organic growth to 7-8%; Life Sciences, Pest and Digital keep growing double digits; surcharges stick after energy normalises so gross margin expands; reported operating margin reaches management's 20% in FY2028 and ~22% by FY2032 (29% EBITDA less SBC and 6% D&A).

bear.rationale: FY2026 is largely booked (+9%), but from FY2027 AI data-centre capex slows and CoolIT stalls near its $550m acquired run-rate (goodwill at risk); energy prices fall and the 10-14% energy surcharge and 5% trade surcharge unwind faster than input costs; Solenis/Diversey and Veolia/Kurita cap pricing in Institutional and Water; organic growth reverts to the 2015-19 rate of ~3%; reported operating margin stalls at ~18% (25% EBITDA); capex stays at 6.5% to defend the installed base. Terminal growth 2.5% and a 18x cap for a slower-growing, more levered business.

scenario_narratives.base: Ecolab's axes are (1) whether the 5-7% organic algorithm holds as surcharges lap, (2) whether the '20% operating margin' target is delivered, and (3) whether the $4.75bn CoolIT bet on AI data-centre liquid cooling earns its cost of capital. Base: FY2026 closes at +10% reported with H2 organic 6-7% and ~19% adjusted margin as guided; CoolIT annualises in FY2027 and is margin-dilutive that year; organic growth fades from 6% to 4% over the decade; reported operating margin reaches ~20% by FY2031 (four years later than management's target); capex settles at 6% of revenue, equal to D&A; working capital absorbs 15c per dollar of growth. Terminal value is bound by the 20x owner-FCF cap (Gordon at 8.0%/3.0% would be 20.6x).
scenario_narratives.bull: CoolIT proves to be the growth engine management describes, compounding 25-30% for five years on hyperscaler liquid-cooling demand and lifting total-company organic growth toward 8%; Life Sciences, Pest Elimination and Digital keep growing double digits; surcharge pricing is retained after energy costs normalise, so gross margin expands beyond 44.4%; operating margin hits 20% in FY2028 and ~22% by FY2032. Growth runs 10.5/9.5/8.0% then fades to 4.5%, EBITDA margin reaches 29%.
scenario_narratives.bear: AI data-centre capex slows after 2026 and CoolIT stalls at roughly its acquired revenue, with the $4.75bn purchase (funded entirely with new debt on a balance sheet already at ~2x net debt/EBITDA) earning well below its cost; falling energy prices unwind the surcharges before input costs fall; competitors cap pricing in the core; organic growth reverts to the ~3% of 2015-19 and margin progression stops at ~18% reported. Value is protected by the recurring installed base, not by growth, so terminal growth is 2.5% and the cap 18x.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default is 15/50/35. Bull weight cut to 25% because it needs three independent things to go right: CoolIT compounding at 25-30%, the 20% margin target landing on time, and surcharges sticking after energy normalises. Bear raised to 25% because the bear case is real and specific: a $4.75bn debt-funded acquisition of an unproven adjacency whose demand is tied to hyperscaler capex, plus surcharge-dependent margins in a year of energy and tariff shocks. No solvency risk (A-/BBB+, interest cover ~9x), so bear does not go higher.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Ecolab is a high-quality, defensive compounder with a recurring razor/razor-blade model, 34 years of dividend growth and demonstrated pricing power, and the market prices it that way at ~34x FY2026 adjusted EPS and ~21x EV/EBITDA. This DCF values the owner cash flows at an 8% USD WACC with SBC fully expensed, the count held flat, terminal value capped at 20x owner FCF, and the CoolIT purchase price deducted in full while its revenue is credited only as it is earned. The required-return table is the honest reading: the current price implies a required return well below the 8% WACC, i.e. the market is paying for either a lower discount rate or a higher exit multiple than this model grants. That is not a claim that the stock will fall; it is a statement that at this price the investor is accepting a bond-like return from a business whose quality is not in question.
key_risks_to_valuation: CoolIT integration and AI data-centre capex durability: the $4.75bn consideration is deducted in full while only ~$550m of revenue is credited; a 25-30% compounder would lift the base materially, a stall would leave goodwill at risk
Surcharge roll-off: 10-14% energy and 5% trade surcharges support FY2026 margins; if they unwind faster than input costs the 20% margin target slips further
Terminal-value dominance: ~60-65% of enterprise value sits in the terminal, bound by the 20x cap; each 0.5pp of WACC moves value roughly 8-10%

Leverage: pro-forma net debt ~$12.8bn (~3x EBITDA before CoolIT contribution) raises refinancing and rate sensitivity; the same WACC is used across scenarios so this risk is carried in the bear weight
FX: roughly half of sales are non-USD; the H1 2026 tailwind (~3-5pp reported vs organic) can reverse
SBC understated: equity-award tax withholding is not tagged in XBRL, so the SBC charge (0.85% of revenue) is modestly low
